topic: The Bridge Between Change and Accumulation: The Relationship Between Derivatives and Integrals
target_audience: High school seniors or first-year university students

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Two Faces of a Curve
lecture_lines: Consider a car moving at a constant velocity.
The flat slope means acceleration is exactly zero.
The shaded area represents the total distance traveled.
animations: Step 1: Draw a horizontal blue line (#58C4DD) representing constant velocity v(t) on a 2D plane.
Step 2: Add a red arrow (#F91717) pointing to the line with the text 'Slope = 0 (Acceleration)'.
Step 3: Gradually fill the rectangular region from t=0 to t=4 under the line with green (#87C2A5) to show 'Area (Distance)'.

sections.title: The Derivative: Capturing the Momentary Change
lecture_lines: Swift's position changes over time along this curve.
Let's focus on his movement at two seconds.
Zooming in, the curve eventually looks perfectly straight.
This tangent line reveals the slope at that moment.
It represents Swift's instantaneous speed at that point.
animations: Step 1: Draw a blue curve (#58C4DD) representing rabbit Swift's position s(t) on a 2D plane.
Step 2: Place a yellow dot (#FFFF00) at t=2 on the curve to mark a specific moment.
Step 3: Scale up the camera view centered at the dot until the curve segment appears as a straight line.
Step 4: Overlay a red tangent line (#F91717) passing through the yellow dot to show the slope.
Step 5: Display the text 's\u2032(2): Instantaneous Speed' in white (#FFFFFF) next to the tangent.

sections.title: The Integral: The Art of Accumulation
lecture_lines: A wavy curve tracks the changing rate of rainfall.
We approximate total water using a few thick rectangles.
Infinite thin rectangles fill the area perfectly.
animations: Step 1: Draw a blue wavy curve (#58C4DD) representing the fluctuating rate of rainfall over time.
Step 2: Create 6 thick green rectangles (#87C2A5) under the curve to approximate the total water collected.
Step 3: Increase the number of rectangles to 100, showing them becoming thinner and perfectly filling the area.

sections.title: The Core Connection: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
lecture_lines: Calculus uses a "Magic Machine" to connect functions.
First, we feed a position function into the machine.
The differentiation operator calculates the rate of change.
Out comes the velocity function, describing the motion.
Integrating this velocity returns us to the original position.
animations: Step 1: Create a white box (#FFFFFF) in the center labeled 'The Magic Machine'.
Step 2: Animate a symbol F(x) moving into the left side of the box.
Step 3: Inside the box, flash a red d/dx operator (#F91717) to represent differentiation.
Step 4: Animate a symbol f(x) moving out of the right side of the box.
Step 5: Show f(x) entering an integral chamber \u222b in blue (#58C4DD) to return to F(x) + C.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Visualization: The Growing Area
lecture_lines: Let the green area represent the accumulated total.
Nudge the boundary forward by a tiny amount, dx.
This creates a thin sliver of new area.
The sliver’s height is determined by the curve’s value.
Thus, the rate of area growth is the function.
animations: Step 1: Plot a blue curve y=f(x) (#58C4DD) and shade the area A(x) under it in green (#87C2A5).
Step 2: Draw a vertical dashed line at position x and another at x + dx.
Step 3: Fill the thin vertical strip between x and x + dx with yellow (#FFFF00) to show area growth.
Step 4: Add labels f(x) for the height and dx for the width of the yellow strip in white (#FFFFFF).

Step 5: Display the formula dA = f(x) \u00b7 dx, concluding that dA/dx = f(x), and place the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/based.svg] icon next to the final result to signify its importance.

sections.title: Practical Application: The Cheetah's Sprint
lecture_lines: We start with the cheetah’s recorded acceleration data.
Integrating acceleration gives the cheetah’s changing velocity.
A second integration calculates the total distance covered.
animations: Step 1: Draw a red acceleration curve a(t) (#F91717) representing a cheetah's sprint.
Step 2: Shade the area under the curve to transform it into a blue velocity graph v(t) (#58C4DD).
Step 3: Animate a small dot moving along a path to represent the cheetah's accumulated distance.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are two sides of one coin.
They function as inverse operations, reversing each other.
Together, they link momentary change to total accumulation.
animations: Step 1: Display the words 'Differentiation' and 'Integration' at opposite sides of the screen in white (#FFFFFF).
Step 2: Draw a circular orange arrow (#FC6255) connecting the two terms to show they are inverses.
Step 3: Display the sequences s \u2192 v \u2192 a and a \u2192 v \u2192 s in blue (#58C4DD) to summarize the loop.
